title: Visible Enclosure Organization of Traditional Zaojing Ceilings in Fu’an, China: Physical References, Internal Articulation, and Ensemble Configurations
content: Traditional zaojing ceilings distinguish visually prominent overhead areas in halls for worship, as-sembly, and performance, yet similar outlines can enclose different arrangements of visible panels and timber members. Using terrestrial laser scanning, field photographs, and existing conditional models, this study examines 64 ceilings in 15 buildings in Fu’an. The comparison addresses physical measurement extent, internal panel articulation, and position within ceiling ensembles. With-in-ceiling analyses show that changing the lower reference changes the enclosure segment represent-ed by geometric indicators. Among 32 ceilings with continuous inclined-panel-foot references (P32), the area within the adopted opening boundary and reference height difference are positively associ-ated (Spearman ρ = 0.824), while covariation among the proportional indicators depends on building composition. Six detailed cases distinguish slope transitions within continuous panels from inde-pendent inner-panel zones; similar relative depths can therefore represent different visible arrange-ments. Across six ensembles comprising 41 ceilings in five buildings, central-to-peripheral or cen-tral-to-flanking relative-depth ratios are 2.687 in Zhaoying Temple and 0.663 in Huang Ancestral Hall. These cases show contrasting relationships between spatial centrality and relative recess depth. The approach describes existing ceiling morphology through explicit physical references and links dimensions, component identities, and spatial positions to their measured or model-derived evidence.
